01 · The world we entered

How do fleets usually work — and how does this organization actually work?

~550

vehicles used daily by several departments — tracked by hand and in separate Excel files

BRD-VMS-003 §4.1 · approximately 550

Imagine managing ~550 vehicles across several departments —
with the information scattered across manual records and Excel files. You need an answer — right now.

VEHICLE X
  • ?Is its license still valid?
  • ?Who is responsible for this vehicle?
  • ?What was its average fuel consumption last month?
  • ?What has this vehicle cost us in maintenance so far?
  • ?Which mission is vehicle X currently assigned to?

If answering these takes more than a few seconds,
you have a visibility problem.

03 · People and ownership

Who are we actually designing these capabilities for?

Team-created personas · based on discovery & analysis
Fleet DirectorEng. Hesham Abdel Hamid

25+ years in fleet & logistics operations · runs ~550 vehicles with a small team · reports to the Head of Authority

“I just want one screen that tells me what needs action today.”

Behaviour

  • Tracks licenses in Excel and paper files, reviewed near the end of each week
  • Follows up daily by phone / WhatsApp with dispatchers
  • Prefers simple, direct information over long meetings

Goals

  • No vehicle stops because of an expired license
  • See fleet availability, maintenance and overdue status clearly
  • Understand fuel and maintenance cost per vehicle

Pain points

  • License expiry can go unnoticed
  • Data is scattered across Excel and paper
  • Hard to see which vehicles are becoming expensive to operate
Operations DirectorMr. Tarek Soliman

15+ years in field operations · field teams request vehicles daily · reports shortages and delays to leadership

“When I request a vehicle in the morning, the right one has to be ready.”

Behaviour

  • Requests vehicles in the morning by phone or WhatsApp
  • Follows field teams mainly from mobile
  • Thinks in terms of service impact and availability

Goals

  • The right vehicle is ready when requested
  • Know request status and expected vehicle availability
  • Resolve shortages quickly so service is not interrupted

Pain points

  • Vehicles can arrive late or become unavailable unexpectedly
  • No clear answer to “when will it arrive?”
  • Replacements can be slow during peak periods

Once we understood their goals and pain points, those needs started becoming features.

05 · The baseline

Verification & Validation

Turning vague requirements into clear, testable ones

Worked exampleF-04Vehicle List, Search & FilterMust · Confirmed
Before verification

Browse and filter the vehicle list by attributes such as type, brand, status, and other key fields.

Issues found
  • “Search” is in the name, but no search fields are defined
  • “Other key fields” is vague, so it can't be tested
  • Several filters at once: AND or OR?
  • Browse undefined: paging, sorting, empty results
  • Archived vehicles and performance not addressed

+ 8 more points in the verification review

After verification Verification-ready

Authorized users can view, search and filter the vehicle list using defined search fields and attributes, with clear handling of empty results and large result sets.

  • SearchVehicle ID · Plate Number · VIN/Chassis · Model
  • FiltersType · Brand · Status
  • LogicMultiple filters use AND · search works with filters
  • BaselineEmpty state · Pagination · Sorting
  • Open points6 marked [CONFIRM] for the stakeholder
ValidationAre we solving the right need?Checked with the stakeholder
VerificationDid we write it the right way?Clear, specific and testable

“Before”: Consolidated Feature List (A04), F-04 · “After”: team verification review, consistent with Module 01 US-04 · Overall validation still partial: BRD sign-off and As-Is confirmation pending (ISS-10)

07 · From requirement to backlog

User Stories & Exception Handling

VMS Project | Example: US-01 — Add Vehicle

User story · US-01

“As a Fleet Director, I want to add a new vehicle with its master data, so that every vehicle in the fleet is held in one central record.”

Trace: F-01 · BR-001 · BRL-13 · NFR-SEC-02
What I defined
  • Required inputs and data types
  • Acceptance criteria
  • Business rules and validation
  • Exception and error-handling scenarios
Acceptance criteria
  1. 1

    Given I have Create permission, When I open Add Vehicle, Then the form shows the required fields: Plate Number, VIN/Chassis, Model, Type, Brand.

  2. 2

    Given all required fields are valid, When I click Save, Then the vehicle is created as Active/Available with its Vehicle ID.

  3. 3

    Given the Plate Number already exists, When I click Save, Then a duplicate error appears and no record is created.

  4. 4

    Given a required field is empty or invalid, When I click Save, Then validation feedback is shown and no record is created.

Exception handling
ScenarioExpected system behavior
1Duplicate Plate Number or VIN/Chassis NumberInline duplicate error; no record is created
2Required field empty or only spacesField highlighted, “This field is required”, entered data kept
3Save clicked twice rapidlyOnly one vehicle record is created
4Network fails during Save“Connection error, please try again”; no partial record, retry allowed
5User lacks Create permissionAccess denied and the attempt is logged

Source: Module 01 Vehicle Management V.02, US-01 · Exception rows 3–4: team exception-handling scenarios
